subject: comp
source: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 syllabus 2026–2028, Cambridge International

weeks.topic: The internet and the World Wide Web: URLs, HTTP and HTTPS
objectives: Distinguish the internet from the World Wide Web
Describe the parts of a URL and the purpose of HTTP and HTTPS

weeks.topic: Web browsers, DNS and cookies
objectives: Explain how a web page is located and displayed using DNS
Compare session and persistent cookies

weeks.topic: Digital currency and blockchain
objectives: Explain the concept of digital currency
Describe how blockchain tracks transactions

weeks.topic: Cyber security threats: malware, phishing, pharming, DDoS and hacking
objectives: Describe common cyber security threats
Explain the aims and effects of each threat

weeks.topic: Cyber security solutions: firewalls, proxy servers, SSL and authentication
objectives: Explain how firewalls and proxy servers protect data
Describe SSL/TLS, two-step verification and anti-malware

weeks.topic: Automated systems: sensors, microprocessors and actuators
objectives: Explain how automated systems use sensors and actuators
Evaluate automated systems in industry, transport and agriculture

weeks.topic: Robotics: characteristics, roles and impact
objectives: Describe the characteristics of a robot
Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of robots

weeks.topic: Artificial intelligence: expert systems and machine learning
objectives: Describe the main characteristics of AI
Explain how expert systems and machine learning work

weeks.topic: Arrays: one-dimensional and two-dimensional
objectives: Declare and use 1D and 2D arrays
Use loops to process arrays

weeks.topic: Procedures, functions, parameters and variable scope
objectives: Write procedures and functions with parameters
Distinguish local and global variables

weeks.topic: Library routines and maintainable programs
objectives: Use MOD, DIV, ROUND, LENGTH and RANDOM
Write maintainable code with meaningful identifiers and comments

weeks.topic: File handling: reading and writing text files
objectives: Open, read, write and close text files
Explain why programs store data in files

weeks.topic: Identifying and correcting errors in algorithms
objectives: Find and correct logic and syntax errors in given algorithms
Explain the purpose of an algorithm

weeks.topic: Writing a complete solution to a scenario problem
objectives: Design a program from a written scenario
Combine arrays, loops, selection and validation

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: internet, cyber security, emerging technologies and programming
objectives: Consolidate theory topics from Term 1
Practise array and subroutine questions

weeks.topic: Databases: single-table databases, fields, records and primary keys
objectives: Define fields, records and primary keys
Choose suitable data types for fields

weeks.topic: SQL: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, SUM and COUNT
objectives: Write SQL queries to search a table
Use ORDER BY, SUM and COUNT

weeks.topic: Boolean logic: logic gates and their symbols
objectives: Recognise NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR and XOR gates
Complete truth tables for single gates

weeks.topic: Logic circuits and truth tables
objectives: Draw logic circuits with up to three inputs
Complete truth tables for logic circuits

weeks.topic: Logic expressions from problem statements and circuits
objectives: Write logic expressions from scenarios
Convert between expressions, circuits and truth tables

weeks.topic: Programming practice: 2D arrays combined with file handling
objectives: Process tabular data stored in files
Read data into 2D arrays and write results back

weeks.topic: Programming practice: modular design with functions and validation
objectives: Break programs into reusable subroutines
Validate user input inside functions

weeks.topic: Tracing complex algorithms with trace tables
objectives: Trace algorithms with nested loops and arrays
Identify the output and purpose of algorithms

weeks.topic: Paper 1 practice: extended explain and compare questions
objectives: Write structured answers to 6–8 mark theory questions
Use technical vocabulary precisely

weeks.topic: Paper 2 practice: the 15-mark programming scenario
objectives: Plan a structured solution before coding
Meet every requirement in the scenario

weeks.topic: Exam technique: pseudocode conventions and command words
objectives: Use Cambridge pseudocode conventions
Interpret command words such as describe, explain and identify

weeks.topic: Mock exams: Paper 1 and Paper 2
objectives: Sit both papers under exam conditions
Analyse results to plan revision

weeks.topic: Revision: data representation and data transmission
objectives: Practise conversions, shifts and file sizes
Revise packets, error detection and encryption

weeks.topic: Revision: hardware and software
objectives: Revise CPU, storage and network hardware
Revise operating systems, interrupts and translators

weeks.topic: Revision: internet, cyber security and emerging technologies
objectives: Revise web technologies and threats
Revise automated systems, robotics and AI

weeks.topic: Revision: algorithm design and programming
objectives: Practise writing and tracing algorithms
Revise arrays, subroutines and file handling

weeks.topic: Revision: databases and Boolean logic
objectives: Practise SQL queries
Practise logic circuits, expressions and truth tables

weeks.topic: Revision: full past-paper practice for both papers
objectives: Complete timed past papers
Compare answers with mark schemes

weeks.topic: Final exams: Paper 1 Computer Systems
objectives: Sit Paper 1 on computer systems theory
Use precise technical terms

weeks.topic: Final exams: Paper 2 Algorithms, Programming and Logic
objectives: Sit Paper 2 on algorithms, programming and logic
Write clear, complete pseudocode

weeks.topic: Exam season: targeted practice between papers
objectives: Review errors from papers already taken
Keep programming skills active

weeks.topic: Exam season close: reflection and bridge to IB Computer Science
objectives: Reflect on the IGCSE course
Preview object-oriented programming and computational thinking
